source_claim: Independently compiled paper-mechanism and execution-contract artifacts can be crossed in a four-cell locked-task trial to distinguish local mechanism value from interface and artifact completion failures.

axes.problem: Determine whether a failed paper-reuse attempt reflects an ineffective paper mechanism or an incomplete execution contract.
axes.mechanism: Typed mechanism and contract artifacts, verifier-closed construction, four same-task counterfactual cells, and mechanism, contract, and interaction contrasts.
axes.insight: Sequentially validating a contract and then measuring utility can misattribute contract rescue to the paper mechanism; the two factors must be independently toggled.
axes.application: Failed or ambiguous paper-derived agent executions on a locked user task.
axes.evaluation_scope: Task-local four-class or not-identifiable diagnosis with paired seeds, cost and regression accounting, and no cross-task pooling.

comparisons.title: SkillFoundry: Automated Mining and Validation of Agent Skills for Scientific Tasks
comparisons.evidence: SkillFoundry validates execution and system contracts before downstream evaluation; it does not cross contract presence with paper-mechanism presence in the same locked task.
comparisons.limitations: Sequential contract validation plus utility is already occupied, so only the independently compiled factorial attribution remains as delta.

comparisons.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
comparisons.evidence: The framework compares whole-skill presence and absence, but does not orthogonalize skill mechanism content from the output and execution contract.
comparisons.limitations: It defeats a broad first-utility-evaluation claim.

comparisons.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
comparisons.evidence: PaperBench separates code, execution, and result evidence in its rubric but does not actively construct the four mechanism-by-contract intervention cells.
comparisons.limitations: Its decomposition is a required baseline for any failure-attribution claim.

comparisons.title: AutoReproduce: Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
comparisons.evidence: AutoReproduce jointly builds and repairs method code plus execution pipeline, leaving mechanism and contract changes entangled for attribution.
comparisons.limitations: It is a stronger reproduction system even if it does not provide the proposed diagnostic.

comparisons.title: Dimension-Level Intent Fidelity Evaluation for Large Language Models: Evidence from Structured Prompt Ablation
comparisons.evidence: Structured ablation is a direct experimental ancestor of factor isolation, but available evidence does not show a paper-mechanism by execution-contract interaction compiler.
comparisons.limitations: The local cache contains only a partial excerpt.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
Two-factor factorial design and interaction analysis are classical and cannot themselves support novelty.
The existing SWE and SNAP repairs are post-hoc pilot evidence; a final evaluation requires prospectively registered new failures.
